text: Opportunity landed in Eagle Crater on Meridiani Planum, Mars, in January 2004.
Opportunity discovered hematite-rich spherules ('blueberries') providing proof of past liquid water on Mars.
Designed for a 90-sol mission, Opportunity explored Mars for nearly 15 years and traversed over 45 kilometers.
Last communication with Opportunity occurred on June 10, 2018 during a global dust storm that blotted out the Sun.
NASA officially declared the Opportunity mission complete on February 13, 2019 after hundreds of recovery attempts.
Opportunity relied on solar arrays for power, making dust accumulation on its panels a persistent operational challenge.
